title: Meet the cone
hint: One point · A round base · A new form

title: Your familiar drawing tools
say: Welcome back! Keep your pencils nearby. An H B pencil is a good choice for light construction. A softer pencil can help you build darker tones later. Have your eraser ready for small adjustments, and keep a clean tissue for optional blending. Use your sketch paper, with room around the drawing.
hint: Pencils · Eraser · Tissue · Sketch paper

title: Make room to change your mind
say: Today, watch how often the teacher checks and adjusts the drawing. Those changes are part of the process. You can do the same. Keep your first marks light, relax your hand, and take each little step at your own pace.
hint: Light marks are easy to adjust

title: Build an upside-down T
say: See the upside-down T? The upright line gives us a centre, and the line across the bottom helps place the base. Together, they give the cone a balanced framework to grow from. Try these light guides with your H B pencil. They do not need to be perfect. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: A centre line and base guide give you a framework.

title: Compare height and width
say: Here is a useful drawing check. See the teacher adjusting the base width? Compare the height with the width, and keep the tip above the centre of the base. Your drawing does not need to be right on the first try. These small corrections help it become more balanced. Try that on your page. I will wait for you.
hint: Keep the cone balanced around its centre.

title: Adjusting is part of drawing
say: Notice the teacher checking the width again, around forty-eight and fifty-eight seconds. The first marks are a starting point. Use your pencil to compare the distances on either side of the centre. A small change can make the proportions more accurate. Make a small adjustment if you want to, then continue.
hint: Compare, adjust, and compare again.

title: Take your time with proportions
say: The teacher is still adjusting, at one minute nineteen and again around one minute thirty. That is normal. Compare your height and base width with the reference on the right. Use your pencil to measure, and change a mark if you need to. You are learning to look, not racing to finish. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Use your pencil to check the right-hand reference.

title: Check both sides of the axis
say: Let us compare with your drawing. Look at the small width marks on either side of the centre line. Compare those distances before drawing the sides. A small correction now is easier than repairing a shaded cone. Try that on your page. I will wait for you.
hint: Compare left and right before joining them.

title: Connect the tip to the base
say: Look at this little detail. The teacher connects the top point to the two outer limits of the base. Keep these construction lines light. They establish the overall taper before the curved base is refined. Make a small adjustment if you want to, then continue.
hint: Light straight guides first.

title: Round the base into an ellipse
say: Here is a useful drawing check. The circular base appears as an ellipse from this viewpoint. Notice the curve across the front. Round the ends gently instead of closing them into sharp points. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Avoid sharp corners at the ends.

say: Watch the last small adjustments. Then compare your drawing with the reference. Keep what is working, and gently adjust anything you want to improve. There is no need to rush.

title: Your practice is showing
say: You have given your cone a balanced framework. Every careful adjustment helped. Let your hand relax for a moment, then we will explore the light.

title: Lift the construction marks
say: Here is a useful drawing check. The teacher is using an eraser to lift construction marks near the base. Remove only the guides you no longer need. Keep the curved outline readable and avoid rubbing hard enough to damage the paper. Try that on your page. I will wait for you.
hint: Erase gently; keep the useful outline.

title: Check the front curve
say: Notice what just changed. Pause and compare the front edge of the base with your drawing. It curves smoothly across the form. Keep that curve consistent so the cone feels round and rests naturally on the surface. Make a small adjustment if you want to, then continue.
hint: One smooth curve, not a flat bottom.

title: Place the light–shadow boundary
say: Your turn to give this a try. This inner line maps where the cone turns away from the light. Notice how it approaches the tip. It is a guide for a tonal transition, not a dark outline to leave on the finished cone. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: The shadow narrows toward the tip.

title: Connect the cast shadow
say: Notice what just changed. The teacher shades the cast shadow beside the base. Keep the shadow connected to the cone, rather than floating away from it. Build the tone with several light passes. Make a small adjustment if you want to, then continue.
hint: The shadow begins at the contact point.

title: Establish the dark side
say: Your turn to give this a try. Build a clear dark area on the side that turns away from the light. Compare this with the still-light area. Keep the difference readable before adding softer middle tones. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Keep the light area clear.

title: Your practice is showing
say: Those darker areas are giving your cone weight. You have moved from a few light guides to a form you can recognise. Keep going, one small layer at a time.

title: Layer your pencil marks
say: Your turn to give this a try. Watch how the teacher returns to the same area with light strokes. Build the dark gradually instead of pressing hard in one pass. This keeps the paper workable and the tone easier to adjust. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Several light passes give you control.

title: Let the marks follow the taper
say: Let us compare with your drawing. Near the tip, the shaded area becomes narrower. Keep your marks controlled as they approach that point. Avoid a heavy knot of graphite at the top. Try that on your page. I will wait for you.
hint: The form narrows as it rises.

title: Build the middle tone
say: Look at this little detail. Now look between the light area and the darker band. These middle tones help the surface turn toward the shadow. Add them gradually so the cone does not look like two flat cut-out shapes. If you need a lighter touch, try an H B or two H pencil. This is a suggestion for your drawing; compare the value rather than pressing harder. Make a small adjustment if you want to, then continue.
hint: Bridge light and shadow gradually.

title: Soften the transition
say: Here is a useful drawing check. Use overlapping light pencil marks to connect neighbouring tones. Keep the light area lighter, and let the transition become smoother. Softening a transition does not mean making the whole cone the same grey. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Blend with pencil strokes before rubbing.

title: Keep the base grounded
say: Notice what just changed. Look at the darker contact along the bottom. It helps the cone sit on the table. Keep this accent controlled, rather than outlining the entire cone with an equally dark line. Try that on your page. I will wait for you.
hint: Compare the contact edge with the side.

title: Your cone is complete
say: You have built the framework, shaped the base, and turned the surface with light and shadow. That is your core drawing complete! The background, tissue blending and final polish are optional extras. You can explore them now, or share your work and move on.

title: Share your cone
say: Choose a clear photo of your drawing, then tap the send button. Wait for the submitted message so you know it has arrived. You can also continue without a photo and return later. Your drawing already counts.

title: Use the background to reveal the edge
say: Let us compare with your drawing. The teacher adds tone outside the light side of the cone. This contrast helps the light edge become visible without a thick outline. Keep the background marks outside the form. Try that on your page. I will wait for you.
hint: Dark beside light makes the form clearer.

title: Keep broad marks consistent
say: Look at this little detail. Notice the broad diagonal strokes around the cone. Use a consistent direction and gentle pressure to establish the surrounding tone. Check that the cone still stands out clearly. Make a small adjustment if you want to, then continue.
hint: Build an even surrounding tone.

title: Check the cast-shadow shape
say: Here is a useful drawing check. Compare the cast shadow with the base. Its darkest contact stays near the object, while the outer area can soften. Avoid turning it into a hard, equally dark border. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Keep it attached; soften farther away.

title: Compare the whole value pattern
say: Notice what just changed. Step back for a moment. Compare the light area, the middle transition, and the shadow. The background should support those differences, not compete with the cone. Try that on your page. I will wait for you.
hint: Light side, turning tone, dark side.

title: Blend gently with tissue
say: Your turn to give this a try. Here the teacher uses tissue over a fingertip to soften the graphite. Use gentle pressure and short controlled movements. Keep a clean part of the tissue over light areas, so you do not drag dark graphite into them. Make a small adjustment if you want to, then continue.
hint: Soften graphite without losing the form.

title: Return to the pencil after blending
say: Let us compare with your drawing. After blending, return to the pencil to strengthen selected tones and edges. Do not redraw every outline. Restore only the details that help the form read clearly. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Restore the structure you still need.

title: Balance the background
say: Look at this little detail. Compare the background on both sides. Adjust it gradually so it supports the lighter and darker parts of the cone. Keep checking the whole drawing instead of darkening one small area too much. Try that on your page. I will wait for you.
hint: Keep attention on the cone.

say: Look at this little detail. These final pencil touches refine the transition near the lower side. Compare neighbouring tones and make small changes. Preserve the difference between the lit surface and the shadow. Make a small adjustment if you want to, then continue.
hint: Small changes can make the curve clearer.

title: Finish the contact edge
say: Here is a useful drawing check. Check the contact at the base one last time. A controlled dark accent anchors the cone. Then step back and compare the tip, the curved side, and the ellipse as one complete form. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: A grounded base, not a heavy outline.

title: Find a cone around you
say: Think of an ice cream cone, a party hat, or the nose of a toy rocket. Where is the point? Where is the round base? You now have a way to begin drawing those shapes. What would you like to try next?

title: You made a cone
say: You looked, measured, adjusted, and kept going. That is how drawing grows. Your cone does not need to be perfect to deserve a celebration. Artchi has a reward for you. Next we will explore how different forms meet.
